groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–2 题
groups.material:
Have you noticed how similar you are to your friends? It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other. We know that friends are more likely to be the same age, gender and ethnic background as each other. Now it seems their brains are alike, too.
Researchers at the University of California scanned the brains of 42 classmates while they watched videos intended to provoke varying responses. Some people might find a romantic scene touching, for instance, while others would feel it was embarrassing. The activity of friends' brains was more similar than that of people who didn't know each other, particularly in regions involved in attention, emotion and language. This similarity was strong enough that it could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not. The relationship probably goes two ways. We are drawn to people who think like us; we then influence their thoughts over time, which may push their brain activity into more closely resembling our own.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 3–4 题
groups.material: Two men who have been best friends for 60 years have just realized they are actually brothers. It's reported that Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald met in the 6th grade at a school in Hawaii. They have been best friends ever since. Alan was given away for adoption soon after he was born, and Walter never knew his father. So recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover more about their ancestry. Walter was astonished to find that he matched with website user Robi 737. He knew immediately that this was his best friend Alan, whose friends call him Robi and flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot. The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart.

groups.title: Section A · 第 3 篇 · 5–7 题
groups.material:
Amid all the election drama, air pollution problems and disease outbreaks, five tourists' good work is being spread online. Yesterday two male and three female tourists were spotted walking the kilometer-long beach, picking up trash. One of the male tourists from Australia commented that although there was a lot of trash, nobody was doing anything. The beach was not as nice or beautiful as it should be. He felt so sad to see such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash. Thus, he and his friends decided to grab a few trash bags and clean it all up.
A man passing by decided to video their good deed and put it on the internet. It was unclear where the rest of the group was from, but they were most likely traveling together. One local woman commented on being embarrassed that tourists were cleaning up their beach. Another mentioned that it was actually the natives who brought food and drinks then left trash all along the island.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 8–11 题
groups.material:
W: Hello Benjamin, Dan and I will be going for a run along the canal Saturday morning. Would you like to join us?
M: I'd love to, but I hurt my ankle last weekend playing football with work colleagues.
W: Oh dear, is it serious?
M: No, not at all. I landed badly during a fall and twisted it a little, but it's no big deal. It's just a little swollen and I should be fine for next Saturday if you still want to go for a jog then.
W: I won't be here next Saturday. I'm going to the zoo.
M: The zoo?
W: Yeah. My little nephew turns six, and he loves the zoo, so the whole family is going.
M: Oh, okay then. I haven't been to a zoo since I was a kid.
W: They are nowhere near as popular as they used to be when we were children. I personally feel sorry for the poor animals stuck in cages, but there's no denying they are fun and educational for children.
M: Do you know if Dan will be around next Saturday?
W: Yeah, I think he will. Just send him a text message. He's always keen on physical activities.
M: That's true. Dan is extremely fit and healthy. He goes to the gym most days, plus tennis two or three times a week.
W: So, what have you been doing to stay busy while you've had that swollen ankle?
M: I've been catching up on some reading. I was given three books over Christmas, and I'm only now getting around to reading them.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
W: Our guest on today's Book Talk is John Black, the author of the new bestseller, Retire Early.
M: Thanks for having me on the show, Lisa.
W: John, your book is getting a lot of attention, partly because you write that most people can retire by 40. Is that realistic?
M: Definitely. When researching this book, I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40.
W: Okay, but how much money does a person need to retire? I've read articles recommending one million dollars as a good figure for retirement.
M: While most financial planners do give numbers, I don't think that's useful, as people are living in different areas with different costs of living, and have different needs and wants, which is why I suggest that people aim for financial independence.
W: What do you mean by financial independence?
M: Having investment income that's greater than monthly expenses.
W: That sounds risky to me. What if an accident happens or you get ill and need medical treatment? Shouldn't people have extra cash for emergencies?
M: Too many people spend their lives working on jobs they hate because they're afraid, so I counsel people to take risks. Retirement doesn't have to be permanent, and if people need to, they can go back to work.
W: But it's not always easy to get back into the workforce after an extended absence.
M: True, but if you keep current with your skills, you will be attracted to employers.
W: Maybe, but how can anyone save enough to retire by 40 when most people can't retire at 60?
M: Simple, by cutting housing, food, and transport expenses, and investing half your monthly income.
W: That sounds impossible.
M: I admit it's difficult, but it has worked for thousands.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
New research from America studies the role that the presence of individuals from different social or racial groups has in influencing consumers' food choices. This research found college students were more likely to choose healthy food in the presence of an observer of a different race, as opposed to an observer from their own race. The same was true when they were with someone from a different university, compared to someone from their own. Researchers say this was because participants anticipated more negative judgment from an outsider group. In contrast, they felt less judged by members of their own group.
In one experiment, participants were offered the choice between candy and fruit as a snack. When in the presence of an unknown student from their own university, only 12 percent of students selected the healthier option. However, this number was 31 percent when in the presence of an unknown student from another university. Other experiments showed similar results based on racial group.
What's the reason for this pattern? The study found that people feel judged to a larger extent by members of other groups. Because of this, they strategically use healthy food choices to make a positive impression. There have been many attempts to help consumers make healthier choices, but consumers often struggle to maintain a healthy diet. This research finds that one way to promote a healthy diet could be to advertise the social benefits of healthy choices.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
For college students under pressure, a dog may be the best stress fighter around, according to the finding of a recent study. "It's a really powerful finding," said Patricia Pendry, who led the study. "Universities are doing a lot of great work trying to help students succeed academically, especially those who may be at risk due to a history of mental health issues or academic and learning issues. This study shows that traditional stress management approaches aren't as effective for this population compared with programs that focus on providing opportunities to interact with therapy dogs."
The researchers measured executive functioning in the students involved in the study. Executive function is a term for the skills one needs to plan, organize, motivate, concentrate and memorize. These are skills students need to succeed in college. The researchers found that students who were most at risk had the most improvements in executive functioning after interacting with therapy dogs. These results remained when researchers followed up six weeks later.
Many universities provide academic stress management programs and workshops. These are traditionally very similar to college classes. They often talk about ways to get more sleep, set goals, or manage stress or anxiety. Pendry acknowledges that these are really important topics and these workshops help typical students succeed. But they're less helpful for struggling students. Pendry believes those students may experience the programs as another lecture and feel even more stressed.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Taking risks in business does not mean going into business blindly and then expecting great results. On the contrary, taking risks in entrepreneurship involves careful planning and hard work. Nobody can really be sure if risks will be met with success, no matter how calculated they may be. But this should not stop you from taking risks, as risks are necessary if you want your business to succeed.
Some risks may not work out, but an optimistic risk-taker will always look at failure as an opportunity to learn. The willingness to experiment with new ideas is key to business growth. As the old saying goes, "Nothing ventured, nothing gained." Failure will teach you how to think and plan strategically. But just remember that not all risks are good ones, and when you fail, learn from it and move forward.
Since most people tend to avoid risk, businesses that are brave enough to take risks already have a competitive advantage. They are the ones setting the standard with new ideas, fresh offers and bold inventions. Risk-takers are best at adapting in difficult times. Simply put, when most individuals stay away from risk, it means less competition for risk-takers. We don't know if you'll achieve what these risk-takers have achieved. But for as long as you want to stay safe, and for as long as you are content with where your business is right now, you will never find out.

questions.prompt: What may be the reason that friends are similar to each other according to the recent research?
options: Their brains work in harmony.
They are generally the same age.
Their interests are quite similar.
They have the same ethnic background.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What may be the reason that friends are similar to each other according to the recent research? 

 【翻译】 根据最近的研究,朋友之间相似的原因可能是什么? 
 A)  他们的大脑协调运作。 
 B)  他们通常年龄相同。 
 C)  他们的兴趣非常相似。 
 D)  他们有相同的族裔背景。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Their brains work in harmony. 
 【定位】 P1 It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other. 
 这可能是因为你们的大脑彼此协同运作。 

 【信号】 因果信号 because 。录音开头先抛问句“有没有发现你和朋友很像“，紧接 It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other —— because 就是把答案点亮的因果信号词，because 后面那句正是“相似的原因“，直接命中题干所问。 

 【替换】 your brains operate in harmony with each other ↔ Their brains work in harmony. operate 换说成 work 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音确实念到 friends are more likely to be the same age，They are generally the same age. 正盗用了这个 same age。但这句前面有 We know that，是“早已知道的旧结论“，并非题干所问的“近期研究发现的相似原因“——原因落在大脑那句，不在同龄这句。  借用原文：friends are more likely to be the same age, gender and ethnic background 

 C) 未提及 Their interests are quite similar. 听起来很合常识，但录音通篇没提“兴趣（interests）“相似，只说了年龄、性别、族裔背景与大脑。它靠的是考生“朋友兴趣相投“的生活常识，而非录音内容，属未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 They have the same ethnic background. 盗用了录音的 ethnic background。和 B 一样，这句出自 We know that friends are more likely to be the same age, gender and ethnic background，是“已知的旧情况“，不是近期研究新发现的相似原因，答非所问。  借用原文：the same age, gender and ethnic background

questions.prompt: What does the news report say about the relationship between friends?
options: It can be touching.
It is hard to predict.
It can work both ways.
It resembles family ties.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the news report say about the relationship between friends? 

 【翻译】 新闻报道关于朋友之间的关系说了什么? 
 A)  它可能令人感动。 
 B)  它难以预测。 
 C)  它可以双向作用。 
 D)  它类似于家庭纽带。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It can work both ways. 
 【定位】 P2 The relationship probably goes two ways. We are drawn to people who think like us; we then influence their thoughts over time, which may push their brain activity into more closely resembling our own. 
 这种关系很可能是双向的。我们被与自己想法相近的人吸引；随后我们又会逐渐影响他们的想法，这可能促使他们的大脑活动变得更接近我们自己的。 

 【信号】 定性句 goes two ways 。录音第二段结尾用 The relationship probably goes two ways 直接给“关系“下定性，后面 We are drawn to people…; we then influence their thoughts 一来一回正是对“双向“的解释。这句“主语就是题干 relationship + 紧跟一个性质判断“的结构，就是答案句信号。 

 【替换】 The relationship probably goes two ways ↔ It can work both ways. two ways 换成 both ways 
 We are drawn to people who think like us; we then influence their thoughts ↔ It can work both ways. 一来一回印证双向 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It can be touching. 盗用了录音的 touching，可那个 touching 出现在 Some people might find a romantic scene touching——是在举例说明“不同人对同一画面反应不同“，说的是“浪漫场景“感人，根本不是在评价“朋友关系“。张冠李戴，答非所问。  借用原文：Some people might find a romantic scene touching, for instance 

 B) 与原文相反 It is hard to predict. 借了录音的 predict。但录音说的是 it could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not——意思是“大脑相似度高到能用来预测两人是不是朋友“，是说“能预测“，根本没说“关系难预测“。选项把“能预测“反着说成了“难预测“，与原文相反。  借用原文：it could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not 

 D) 未提及 It resembles family ties. 听着像那么回事，但录音全程没把朋友关系比作“家庭纽带（family ties）“，只说了关系“双向“。它纯靠考生自行联想，录音无任何对应，属未提及。

questions.prompt: What did both Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald attempt to do on DNA matching websites?
options: Search for their half-brothers.
Identify their biological fathers.
Find out more about their ancestry.
See whether they are actually related.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did both Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald attempt to do on DNA matching websites? 

 【翻译】 Alan Robinson 和 Walter MacDonald 在 DNA 匹配网站上都试图做什么? 
 A)  寻找他们同父异母的兄弟。 
 B)  确认他们的生父身份。 
 C)  了解更多关于他们祖先的信息。 
 D)  查看他们是否真的有血缘关系。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Find out more about their ancestry. 
 【定位】 P1 So recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover more about their ancestry. 
 所以最近，他们俩各自在DNA配对网站上做了尝试，想多了解一些自己的家世血统。 

 【信号】 题干原词attempt复现+目的句 。题干问 attempt to do，录音里恰好出现 made separate attempts on DNA matching websites，attempt 和 DNA matching websites 原词对上，紧跟其后的 to discover more about their ancestry 用 to do 带出目的——这个‘题干关键词复现 + to do 目的句’就是答案信号。 

 【替换】 to discover more about their ancestry ↔ Find out more about their ancestry. discover换成find out，ancestry原样 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说去 Search for their half-brothers.(寻找同父异母的兄弟)。录音确实出现 they are actually brothers‘他们其实是兄弟’，A 盗用了 brothers 这个词，但录音里这是新闻最后揭晓的真相，不是他俩上网时‘想去找的目标’——而且他们是同母兄弟、不是 half-brothers，张冠李戴。  借用原文：they are actually brothers 

 B) 原词陷阱 B 说去 Identify their biological fathers.(确认亲生父亲)。录音有 Walter never knew his father，B 盗用了 father 一词，但这只是介绍背景，两人上网的目的写得很清楚是 discover more about their ancestry(查家世)，不是专门去认父亲。  借用原文：Walter never knew his father 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 说去 See whether they are actually related.(看看俩人是否真有亲属关系)。录音里 they are actually brothers 用了 actually 一词，D 盗用了 actually 并改写成 related，可他们上网时压根不知道彼此有血缘、不是‘去验证是否有关系’，验出是兄弟是意外结果，不是上网动机。  借用原文：they are actually brothers
questions.spoken_text: What did both Alan Robinson and Walter Macdonald attempt to do on DNA matching websites?

questions.prompt: What did the news report say about Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald?
options: They were both given up for adoption.
They were born to the same mother.
They flew 737 airplanes as pilots.
They were both 60 years of age.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the news report say about Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald? 

 【翻译】 新闻报道关于 Alan Robinson 和 Walter MacDonald 说了什么? 
 A)  他们都被送去领养了。 
 B)  他们是同一个母亲所生。 
 C)  他们作为飞行员驾驶 737 飞机。 
 D)  他们都是 60 岁。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They were born to the same mother. 
 【定位】 P1 The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart. 
 这两个人是同一个母亲所生，出生时间相差15个月。 

 【信号】 结尾收束句给出血缘真相 。新闻把最关键的血缘结论放在末句 The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart——新闻报道常把核心事实或结局压在结尾，这个‘篇末收束’位置就是答案信号，born to the same mother 与选项 B 直接对应。 

 【替换】 born to the same mother ↔ They were born to the same mother. 原句几乎照搬主语换成They 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 说两人 They were both given up for adoption.(都被送养)。录音里确有 Alan was given away for adoption，A 盗用了 adoption，但录音只说 Alan 一个人被送养，A 却说成 both(两个人都)，把范围从一人扩大到两人，与原文不符。  借用原文：Alan was given away for adoption 

 C) 张冠李戴 C 说两人 They flew 737 airplanes as pilots.(都当飞行员开737)。录音念到了 flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot，C 盗用了 737 和 pilot 这两个醒目词，但 he 指的只是 Alan 一人，C 说成 They(两人都飞)，把一人之事安到两人头上。  借用原文：flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot 

 D) 偷换概念 D 说两人 They were both 60 years of age.(都60岁)。录音开头有 best friends for 60 years，D 盗用了数字 60，但这60是‘做了60年好朋友’，是友谊的年数，不是两人的年龄；偷换了60所修饰的对象。  借用原文：best friends for 60 years
questions.spoken_text: What did the news report say about Alan Robinson and Walter Macdonald?

questions.prompt: Why did one of the male tourists feel sad?
options: One of his friends was caught littering.
Other tourists refused to join in the cleanup.
The beautiful beach was spoiled with lots of trash.
The kilometer-long beach was practically deserted.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why did one of the male tourists feel sad? 

 【翻译】 为什么其中一位男性游客感到难过? 
 A)  他的一位朋友因乱扔垃圾被抓到。 
 B)  其他游客拒绝参加清理活动。 
 C)  美丽的海滩被大量垃圾破坏了。 
 D)  这片长达一公里的海滩几乎荒无一人。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The beautiful beach was spoiled with lots of trash. 
 【定位】 P1 He felt so sad to see such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash. 
 他看到如此美丽的地方却被这么多垃圾弄得脏乱不堪，感到非常难过。 

 【信号】 feel sad 与题干同词直接命中 。答案句直接出现题干里的 He felt so sad，紧跟其后的 to see such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash 就是难过的原因；听到与题干情绪词同样的‘sad’，那一句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash ↔ The beautiful beach was spoiled with lots of trash 同义改写：美景被垃圾糟蹋 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 项借用录音里的 his friends 一词，但原文只说他和朋友一起去捡垃圾，从没说‘朋友被抓乱扔垃圾’，是把出现过的原词拼成一个录音根本没说的情节。  借用原文：he and his friends decided to grab a few trash bags 

 B) 未提及 录音说的是‘nobody was doing anything’（没人去管这些垃圾），并非‘其他游客拒绝加入清理’；‘refused to join in’这一情节录音从未出现，属凭空捏造。 
 D) 与原文相反 D 项盗用录音里的 kilometer-long beach，却说海滩‘practically deserted（几乎空无一人）’；而录音强调的是海滩满是垃圾、不够美，与‘空无一人’语义不符，方向反了。  借用原文：Yesterday two male and three female tourists were spotted walking the kilometer-long beach

questions.prompt: Who put the good deed video on the internet?
options: A passerby.
A local woman.
The beach authorities.
One of the five tourists.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Who put the good deed video on the internet? 

 【翻译】 谁把这段善举视频上传到了网上? 
 A)  一位路人。 
 B)  一位当地妇女。 
 C)  海滩管理部门。 
 D)  五位游客中的一位。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） A passerby. 
 【定位】 P2 A man passing by decided to video their good deed and put it on the internet. 
 一名路过的男子决定把他们的善举拍下来并发布到网上。 

 【信号】 动作 put it on the internet 与题干同动作 。答案句出现与题干同样的动作 put it on the internet，前面的主语 A man passing by 就是施动者；听到题干里的关键动作时，紧抓它的主语即可锁定答案。 

 【替换】 A man passing by ↔ A passerby 短语压缩成单词 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 B 项盗用录音里的 One local woman，但这位本地女子做的是‘评论说自己很尴尬’，并非上传视频；把别人做的事安到她头上，属人物错位。  借用原文：One local woman commented on being embarrassed that tourists were cleaning up their beach 

 C) 未提及 录音通篇没出现‘beach authorities（海滩管理方）’这个角色，上传视频的也不是任何官方机构，属凭空捏造的身份。 
 D) 张冠李戴 D 项盗用录音里的‘游客’，游客确实是事件主角、在捡垃圾，但发视频到网上的是路过男子而非游客中的某人；把上传动作错记到游客身上。  借用原文：they were most likely traveling together

questions.prompt: Why did one local woman say she was embarrassed?
options: The tourists' good deed was not noticed by the locals.
Some natives were selling poor-quality food to tourists.
The number of tourists to the beach is on a steady decline.
It was tourists not natives who were cleaning up the beach.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why did one local woman say she was embarrassed? 

 【翻译】 为什么一位当地妇女说她感到尴尬? 
 A)  游客的善举没有被当地人注意到。 
 B)  一些本地人向游客出售劣质食品。 
 C)  前往海滩的游客数量持续下降。 
 D)  清理海滩的是游客而不是本地人。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It was tourists not natives who were cleaning up the beach. 
 【定位】 P2 One local woman commented on being embarrassed that tourists were cleaning up their beach. 
 一名本地女子评论说，她为游客在清理他们本地的海滩这件事感到尴尬。 

 【信号】 embarrassed that 直接引出原因 。答案句出现题干同词 embarrassed，紧跟的 that tourists were cleaning up their beach 由 that 直接引出尴尬的原因；听到 embarrassed 后那句 that 从句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 that tourists were cleaning up their beach ↔ It was tourists not natives who were cleaning up the beach 补出隐含对照：游客而非本地人 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 项说‘游客善举没被本地人注意到’，但录音里本地女子明明注意到了才会尴尬，路人还拍了视频，恰恰说明被注意到了；‘not noticed’与录音事实相反。  借用原文：One local woman commented on being embarrassed 

 B) 偷换概念 B 项盗用录音里的 food and drinks，但原文是说本地人‘带来食物饮料后留下垃圾’，绝非‘卖劣质食物给游客’；把‘带来食物乱丢垃圾’偷换成‘卖劣质食物’。  借用原文：it was actually the natives who brought food and drinks then left trash all along the island 

 C) 未提及 录音通篇没提‘游客数量在持续下降’这一信息，本题谈的是清理海滩与尴尬，与游客增减无关，属凭空捏造的全新话题。

questions.prompt: Why can't the man go for a run Saturday morning?
options: He has to play football with workmates.
He has got some books to read.
He is going to visit a friend.
He is physically unfit for it.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why can't the man go for a run Saturday morning? 

 【翻译】 为什么男士周六早上不能去跑步? 
 A)  他必须和同事踢足球。 
 B)  他有一些书要读。 
 C)  他要去拜访一位朋友。 
 D)  他的身体状况不适合跑步。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） He is physically unfit for it. 
 【定位】 P2 I'd love to, but I hurt my ankle last weekend playing football with work colleagues. 
 我很想去，但我上周末和同事踢足球时弄伤了脚踝。 

 【信号】 转折 but 后才是真理由 。男士先说 I'd love to（很想去）是客套，紧跟的 but 才转出真正原因——I hurt my ankle，所以答案句落在 but 之后。 

 【替换】 I hurt my ankle ↔ He is physically unfit for it. 具体伤情概括成"身体不适合" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 He has to play football with workmates. 把原文里的 playing football with work colleagues 原词搬来，但原文是说"踢球时受了伤"、不是"周六要去踢球"，听到 football 就选会落进陷阱。  借用原文：playing football with work colleagues 

 B) 张冠李戴 选项 He has got some books to read. 说的是他后面提到的读书 I've been catching up on some reading，那是第11题的内容，与"为何不能去跑步"无关，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：I've been catching up on some reading 

 C) 未提及 选项 He is going to visit a friend. 在对话里根本没出现，男士不能去跑步的理由是脚伤，不是去看朋友，纯属编造。

questions.prompt: Why is the woman's whole family going to the zoo next Saturday?
options: To teach kids about animal protection.
To learn how popular zoos could be.
To see some rare animals in cages.
To give her little nephew a treat.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why is the woman's whole family going to the zoo next Saturday? 

 【翻译】 为什么女士全家下周六要去动物园? 
 A)  教孩子们动物保护知识。

 我的小侄子要满六岁了，他很喜欢动物园，所以全家一起去。 

 【信号】 因果 so 引出去的原因 。so the whole family is going 里的 so 把前因"小侄子过六岁生日、又喜欢动物园"和后果"全家去"连起来，so 之前就是"为什么去"的答案。 

 【替换】 My little nephew turns six, and he loves the zoo ↔ To give her little nephew a treat. 为侄子庆生=给侄子一份开心 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 To teach kids about animal protection. 借了女士后面说的 they are fun and educational for children 里的 educational，但原文只说动物园对孩子有趣又有教育意义，从没说全家去是为了"教孩子动物保护"，是把原词拔高到原文没说的目的。  借用原文：they are fun and educational for children 

 B) 原词陷阱 选项 To learn how popular zoos could be. 套用了 They are nowhere near as popular as they used to be 里的 popular，但那只是女士顺口评论动物园不如从前受欢迎，绝不是全家去的目的。  借用原文：They are nowhere near as popular as they used to be 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 To see some rare animals in cages. 借了 the poor animals stuck in cages 里的 cages，但原文是女士同情笼中动物，没说去看"珍稀"动物，rare 更是凭空添加。  借用原文：the poor animals stuck in cages

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Dan from the man's description?
options: He enjoys excellent health.
He is keen on extreme sports.
He coaches tennis players every week.
He spends most of his time in the gym.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about Dan from the man's description? 

 【翻译】 从男士的描述中我们了解到Dan的什么情况? 
 A)  他身体非常健康。 
 B)  他热衷于极限运动。 
 C)  他每周指导网球运动员。 
 D)  他大部分时间都在健身房度过。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） He enjoys excellent health. 
 【定位】 P12 Dan is extremely fit and healthy. He goes to the gym most days, plus tennis two or three times a week. 
 Dan 非常健壮、健康。他几乎每天去健身房，外加每周打两三次网球。 

 【信号】 直接给出对 Dan 的总评 。男士 Dan is extremely fit and healthy 是对 Dan 的直接定性评价，后面 gym、tennis 都是佐证，这句总评就是答案句。 

 【替换】 Dan is extremely fit and healthy ↔ He enjoys excellent health. extremely fit and healthy = excellent health 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 选项 He is keen on extreme sports. 把 Dan 的运动夸大为"极限运动"，原文只说他常去健身房、打网球，从没提 extreme sports，属无中生有。 
 C) 偷换概念 选项 He coaches tennis players every week. 搬来原文的 tennis 和 a week，但原文是 Dan 自己"打"网球 plus tennis two or three times a week，不是"教"网球选手，把"打"偷换成"教"。  借用原文：plus tennis two or three times a week 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 He spends most of his time in the gym. 借了 He goes to the gym most days 里的 gym 和 most，但原文是"多数日子去健身房"，选项偷偷改成"把大部分时间花在健身房"，频率被夸大成时长。  借用原文：He goes to the gym most days

questions.prompt: What has the man been doing since last weekend?
options: Tending to his swollen ankle.
Concentrating on reading.
Writing three book reports.
Planning Christmas celebrations.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has the man been doing since last weekend? 

 【翻译】 男士从上周末以来一直在做什么? 
 A)  照料他肿胀的脚踝。 
 B)  专心阅读。 
 C)  写三篇读书报告。 
 D)  计划圣诞节庆祝活动。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Concentrating on reading. 
 【定位】 P14 I've been catching up on some reading. I was given three books over Christmas, and I'm only now getting around to reading them. 
 我一直在补读一些书。圣诞节别人送了我三本书，我现在才腾出空来读它们。 

 【信号】 I've been doing 直接应答 。女士问他脚伤期间在干嘛，男士直接以 I've been catching up on some reading 应答，被问者的这句应答就是答案句，与题干时态对应。 

 【替换】 I've been catching up on some reading ↔ Concentrating on reading. catching up on reading = concentrating on reading 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 Tending to his swollen ankle. 借了女士问句里的 that swollen ankle，但脚踝肿只是他读书的背景，他并没说"一直在护理脚踝"，把背景说成正在做的活动。  借用原文：that swollen ankle 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 Writing three book reports. 搬来原文的 I was given three books 里的 three 和 books，但原文是别人送他三本书"读"，不是他"写三份读书报告"，把"读书"偷换成"写报告"。  借用原文：I was given three books over Christmas 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 Planning Christmas celebrations. 借了 over Christmas 里的 Christmas，但原文 Christmas 只是"圣诞期间收到书"的时间状语，他并没在"筹备圣诞庆祝"，纯属对原词的曲解。  借用原文：over Christmas

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man's book published recently?
options: It is being debated by hundreds of retirees.
It is attracting many people's attention.
It partly records his own experience.
It argues for postponing retirement.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the man's book published recently? 

 【翻译】 关于这位男士最近出版的书，我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  数百名退休人员正在对它进行讨论。 
 B)  它正在吸引许多人的关注。 
 C)  它部分记录了他自己的经历。 
 D)  它主张推迟退休。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It is attracting many people's attention. 
 【定位】 P3 John, your book is getting a lot of attention, partly because you write that most people can retire by 40. 
 约翰，你的书正受到很多关注，部分原因是你在书里写道大多数人能在 40 岁退休。 

 【信号】 主持人开场对书的正面定性句 。主持人介绍书时直接给出定性：your book is getting a lot of attention。这种"主持人开场对作品的概括"就是介绍类细节题的答案信号——它把书的核心特点一句点明。 

 【替换】 getting a lot of attention ↔ attracting many people's attention "获得关注"换说成"吸引关注" 

 【排除】 C) 偷换概念 录音里作者说 I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40，是"采访了几百人"，并没说书"记录他自己的经历"；C 把"研究别人"偷换成"写他自己"，答非所问。  借用原文：I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40 

 D) 与原文相反 录音说书主张 most people can retire by 40，是"提前到 40 岁退休"，而 D 说书主张"推迟退休"(postponing retirement)，正好反了。这是把"提前"听成"推迟"的反向陷阱。  借用原文：most people can retire by 40 

 A) 原词陷阱 录音里 hundreds 来自 I interviewed hundreds of people，指作者"采访了几百人"，A 却说书"正被几百名退休者讨论"(debated by hundreds of retirees)，把"被采访的人"偷换成"在讨论书的人"，是听到 hundreds 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40

questions.prompt: What do the articles the woman read recommend?
options: One should foresee a financial crisis.
One should trust financial planners, figures.
One should have one million dollars to retire.
One should start saving as early as possible.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the articles the woman read recommend? 

 【翻译】 这位女士读到的文章建议什么？ 
 A)  人们应该预见到金融危机。 
 B)  人们应该相信理财规划师的数据。 
 C)  人们应该有一百万美元才能退休。 
 D)  人们应该尽早开始储蓄。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） One should have one million dollars to retire. 
 【定位】 P5 I've read articles recommending one million dollars as a good figure for retirement. 
 我读过一些文章，推荐一百万美元作为退休的合适数额。 

 【信号】 女士转述文章的 recommend 句 。女士说 I've read articles recommending one million dollars，动词 recommend 与题干 recommend 完全对应，这句"女士转述文章推荐什么"就是答案信号——题目问的正是这个来源。 

 【替换】 one million dollars as a good figure for retirement ↔ have one million dollars to retire "一百万作合适数额"="应有一百万才退休" 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 financial planners 确实在录音出现 most financial planners do give numbers，但那是嘉宾说"规划师爱给数字、我觉得没用"，文章并没"推荐相信规划师"。B 把原词搬来、又把内容安错了人(文章 vs 规划师)。  借用原文：most financial planners do give numbers, I don't think that's useful 

 D) 答非所问 "尽早储蓄"听着像理财常识，但录音里文章推荐的是"一百万这个数额"，并没说"尽早储蓄"；至于储蓄、投资是嘉宾在后面(P14)讲的做法，不是"女士读的文章"推荐的。D 答非所问。  借用原文：investing half your monthly income 

 A) 未提及 选项 A 的 financial crisis 借了话题里"financial"的语感，但文章推荐的是具体金额，从没让人"预见金融危机"；录音通篇也没出现"危机"的意思。A 是听到 financial 就联想出来的干扰。

questions.prompt: What does the man say about retirement?
options: It doesn't need to be permanent.
It shouldn't be considered risky.
It helps to reduce travel expenses.
It is the way to quit a job one hates.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about retirement? 

 【翻译】 这位男士对退休有何看法？ 
 A)  它不必是永久性的。 
 B)  它不应该被认为有风险。 
 C)  它有助于减少旅行开支。 
 D)  它是辞去自己讨厌的工作的方式。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It doesn't need to be permanent. 
 【定位】 P10 Retirement doesn't have to be permanent, and if people need to, they can go back to work. 
 退休不一定是永久的，如果有需要，人们可以重新回去工作。 

 【信号】 男士对退休下的直接定性句 。男士直接断言 Retirement doesn't have to be permanent，这是他对"退休"本身的一句正面定义，又用 they can go back to work 加以说明，是"他怎么说退休"的直接答案信号。 

 【替换】 Retirement doesn't have to be permanent ↔ It doesn't need to be permanent doesn't have to=doesn't need to 
 they can go back to work ↔ doesn't need to be permanent "能回去工作"佐证"不必永久" 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 risky 来自女士 That sounds risky to me 和男士 I counsel people to take risks——男士是"劝人去冒险"，承认有风险；B 却说退休"不该被视为有风险"，意思反了，是听到 risk 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：I counsel people to take risks 

 D) 原词陷阱 a job they hate 确实出现在 spend their lives working on jobs they hate，但那是男士解释"很多人因恐惧而困在烂工作里"的背景，不是给退休下定义；D 把这句背景说成"退休就是辞掉烂工作的途径"，答非所问。  借用原文：spend their lives working on jobs they hate 

 C) 未提及 C 说退休"有助减少差旅开支"(reduce travel expenses)，录音里 transport 出现在 cutting housing, food, and transport expenses，那是"怎样攒钱"的省钱办法，与"退休本身是什么"无关，更没说退休能省路费。C 属嫁接他处原词的无中生有。  借用原文：cutting housing, food, and transport expenses

questions.prompt: How does the man say his proposal about retirement can be carried out?
options: By keeping close contact with one's employers.
By retiring when one reaches sixty years old.
By investing half of one's monthly income.
By following the counsel of financial planners.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does the man say his proposal about retirement can be carried out? 

 【翻译】 这位男士说他关于退休的提议可以如何实施？ 
 A)  通过与雇主保持密切联系。 
 B)  通过在年满六十岁时退休。 
 C)  通过投资月收入的一半。 
 D)  通过遵循理财规划师的建议。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） By investing half of one's monthly income. 
 【定位】 P14 Simple, by cutting housing, food, and transport expenses, and investing half your monthly income. 
 很简单，靠削减住房、饮食和交通开支，并拿出月收入的一半去投资。 

 【信号】 男士回答"怎么做到"的 by 操作句 。面对女士"怎么可能 40 岁退休"的追问，男士直接答 by cutting housing, food, and transport expenses, and investing half your monthly income，这句"by + 一串具体动作"就是 How 类题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 investing half your monthly income ↔ investing half of one's monthly income 几乎原句对应的"投月收入一半" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 employers 出现在 you will be attracted to employers，那是男士讲"保持技能就能被雇主青睐、好重返职场"，回应的是"能否回去工作"，不是"怎么攒钱提前退休"；A 把它说成"靠和雇主保持密切联系来实现退休"，答非所问。  借用原文：if you keep current with your skills, you will be attracted to employers 

 B) 与原文相反 sixty 来自女士的反问 most people can't retire at 60，意在质疑"连 60 都退不了，怎么 40 退"；B 却说"靠 60 岁退休来实现"，方向反了——男士主张的是 40 岁提前退，不是等到 60。  借用原文：how can anyone save enough to retire by 40 when most people can't retire at 60 

 D) 与原文相反 financial planners 和 counsel 都在录音里——但男士对规划师是 I don't think that's useful，并不让人"听规划师的"；counsel 是他"劝人冒险"(I counsel people to take risks)，不是"听规划师劝告"。D 把原词拼到一起，方向与男士立场相反。  借用原文：While most financial planners do give numbers, I don't think that's useful

questions.prompt: What was the finding of the new research from America about consumers' food choices?
options: They tended to be easily anticipated by those belonging to their own race.
They tended to be arbitrarily judged by individuals of opposing groups.
They were readily shared among members of the same social or racial group.
They were influenced by the presence of someone from an outsider group.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What was the finding of the new research from America about consumers' food choices? 

 【翻译】 来自美国的新研究关于消费者食物选择的发现是什么? 
 A)  它们往往容易被属于同一种族的人预测。 
 B)  它们往往被对立群体的个体任意评判。 
 C)  它们在同一社会或种族群体的成员之间容易共享。 
 D)  它们受到来自外部群体的某人在场的影响。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They were influenced by the presence of someone from an outsider group. 
 【定位】 P1 This research found college students were more likely to choose healthy food in the presence of an observer of a different race, as opposed to an observer from their own race. 
 这项研究发现，与本族观察者在场相比，大学生在不同种族的观察者在场时更可能选择健康食物。 

 【信号】 结论标志词 found 。录音 This research found 直接亮出研究结论，found 后面跟的就是研究发现，这是篇章交代核心结论的标志，听到 found/showed 这类词就知道答案句来了。 

 【替换】 in the presence of an observer of a different race ↔ influenced by the presence of someone from an outsider group 下位换上位 
 were more likely to choose healthy food ↔ were influenced 详述换概括 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 用了录音后文 participants anticipated more negative judgment 里的 anticipated 一词，但把它扭成易被同族人预料，与研究发现毫无关系，是听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：participants anticipated more negative judgment 

 B) 偷换概念 B 说食物选择被对立群体的个人任意评判，借了录音 they felt less judged by members of their own group 的 judge 概念，但研究发现的是选择被在场者影响，不是选择本身被评判，偷换了概念。  借用原文：they felt less judged by members of their own group 

 C) 与原文相反 C 说食物选择在同族群体内易被共享，但录音 they felt less judged by members of their own group 讲的是同族在场时人感觉评判更少、影响更小，根本没说共享选择，且方向与研究重点（外群体才带来改变）相反。  借用原文：they felt less judged by members of their own group
questions.spoken_text: What was the finding of the new research from America about consumers' food choices?

questions.prompt: When did 31 percent of students in the experiment select the healthier option?
options: When they tried to make a positive impression on the researchers.
When an unknown student from another university was present.
When an experimenter from the research team took notice.
When they were offered both candy and fruit as a snack.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 When did 31 percent of students in the experiment select the healthier option? 

 【翻译】 实验中百分之三十一的学生在什么时候选择了更健康的选项? 
 A)  当他们试图给研究人员留下积极印象时。 
 B)  当一名来自另一所大学的陌生学生在场时。 
 C)  当研究团队的一名实验人员注意到时。 
 D)  当他们被提供糖果和水果作为零食时。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） When an unknown student from another university was present. 
 【定位】 P2 However, this number was 31 percent when in the presence of an unknown student from another university. 
 然而，当一名来自另一所大学的陌生学生在场时，这个数字是 31%。 

 【信号】 数字与 when 条件绑定 。录音 this number was 31 percent when in the presence of an unknown student from another university 把 31 percent 与 when 引导的在场条件直接绑在一起，听到目标数字就顺势抓它后面的 when 从句，即答案条件。 

 【替换】 an unknown student from another university ↔ an unknown student from another university 条件原句对应 
 in the presence of ↔ was present 名词短语换动词 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 说学生想给研究者留好印象，录音只说他们 use healthy food choices to make a positive impression，但针对的是外群体在场者，不是 researchers，录音从未提对研究者留好印象这个条件，属无中生有。 
 C) 原词陷阱 C 借了录音多次出现的 research/experimenter 概念，编出研究团队的实验员注意到时，但 31 percent 绑定的是外校学生在场，与实验员留意无关，是听到 research 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：Other experiments showed similar results 

 D) 张冠李戴 D 说同时提供糖果和水果作零食时，candy 和 fruit 确是录音 participants were offered the choice between candy and fruit as a snack 的原词，但这是整个实验的设置，对应 12% 与 31% 两种情境，不专属 31%，把背景条件错安成 31% 的专属触发，张冠李戴。  借用原文：participants were offered the choice between candy and fruit as a snack
questions.spoken_text: When did 31% of students in the experiment select the healthier option?

questions.prompt: How could a healthy diet be promoted according to the findings of the new research?
options: By advertising its social benefits.
By teaching consumers diet strategies.
By supporting struggling consumers.
By maintaining its positive image.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How could a healthy diet be promoted according to the findings of the new research? 

 【翻译】 根据新研究的发现,如何促进健康饮食? 
 A)  通过宣传其社会益处。 
 B)  通过向消费者传授饮食策略。 
 C)  通过支持处境艰难的消费者。 
 D)  通过维持其正面形象。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） By advertising its social benefits. 
 【定位】 P3 This research finds that one way to promote a healthy diet could be to advertise the social benefits of healthy choices. 
 这项研究发现，推动健康饮食的一种方式可能是宣传健康选择的社会益处。 

 【信号】 建议句 one way to…could be to 。录音 one way to promote a healthy diet could be to advertise the social benefits 用 one way to…could be to 这一建议句式给出对策，这是篇章结尾提对策的信号，听到就锁定后面的方法。 

 【替换】 advertise the social benefits of healthy choices ↔ advertising its social benefits 动词变动名词 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 B 说教消费者饮食策略，录音虽提到 many attempts to help consumers make healthier choices，但从未说具体方法是教饮食策略，这个手段是凭空添加的，属未提及。 
 C) 原词陷阱 C 说支持苦苦挣扎的消费者，借了录音 consumers often struggle to maintain a healthy diet 的 struggle 一词，但那只是描述现状，不是研究给出的对策，是听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：consumers often struggle to maintain a healthy diet 

 D) 张冠李戴 D 说维持其正面形象，借了录音 make a positive impression 里的 positive 概念，但那讲的是个人用健康选择给自己留好印象，不是推动健康饮食的对策，张冠李戴。  借用原文：they strategically use healthy food choices to make a positive impression
questions.spoken_text: How could a healthy diet be promoted according to the findings of the new research?

questions.prompt: What does the recent study led by Patricia Pendry aim to examine?
options: The academic and learning issues struggling students encounter.
The risk students face due to a history of mental health problems.
The effect of interacting with therapy dogs on students under pressure.
The work universities are doing to help students succeed academically
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the recent study led by Patricia Pendry aim to examine? 

 【翻译】 Patricia Pendry领导的最新研究旨在考察什么? 
 A)  处境困难的学生遇到的学业和学习问题。 
 B)  学生因心理健康问题史而面临的风险。 
 C)  与治疗犬互动对压力下学生的影响。 
 D)  大学为帮助学生在学业上取得成功所做的工作。 

 【答案】 C （主旨题） The effect of interacting with therapy dogs on students under pressure. 
 【定位】 P1 This study shows that traditional stress management approaches aren't as effective for this population compared with programs that focus on providing opportunities to interact with therapy dogs. 
 这项研究表明，对这一人群而言，传统的压力管理方法不如那些专注于提供与治疗犬互动机会的项目有效。 

 【信号】 总结句 This study shows 。This study shows that 是篇章里的"结论/点题"信号——一旦听到"这项研究表明……"，后面紧跟的就是研究的核心发现/目的，这正是主旨题的答案落点。 

 【替换】 programs that focus on providing opportunities to interact with therapy dogs ↔ The effect of interacting with therapy dogs on students under pressure 动作短语→名词化概括 
 For college students under pressure ↔ students under pressure 几乎原词对应的对象 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项盗用了录音里的 academic and learning issues 原词，但那只是描述"哪类学生处于风险"的背景信息，不是研究要考察的内容。听到原词就选会中招。  借用原文：academic and learning issues 

 B) 原词陷阱 选项搬用了录音的 a history of mental health issues，但那同样是在说明"哪些学生有风险"的铺垫，不是研究目的。把背景当主旨就错了。  借用原文：a history of mental health issues 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项几乎照搬录音 Universities are doing a lot of great work trying to help students succeed academically，但那是 Pendry 在铺垫"大学在做很多帮扶工作"的大背景，不是"这项研究"本身要考察的内容；研究聚焦的是治疗犬，不是泛泛的大学帮扶工作。  借用原文：Universities are doing a lot of great work trying to help students succeed academically
questions.spoken_text: What does the recent study led by Patricia Pendry aim to examine?

questions.prompt: What did the new study measure in the participants?
options: Their communicative skills.
Their executive functioning.
Their academic networking.
Their leadership capacities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the new study measure in the participants? 

 【翻译】 这项新研究测量了参与者的什么? 
 A)  他们的沟通技能。 
 B)  他们的执行功能。 
 C)  他们的学术人际网络。 
 D)  他们的领导能力。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Their executive functioning. 
 【定位】 P2 The researchers measured executive functioning in the students involved in the study. 
 研究人员测量了参与研究的学生的执行功能。 

 【信号】 原词 measured 直接领出宾语 。录音用 The researchers measured executive functioning，measured 这个动词与题干 measure 完全对应，紧跟其后的宾语就是答案，是最直接的细节定位信号。 

 【替换】 measured executive functioning ↔ Their executive functioning 原词直接对应 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 communicative skills（沟通能力）录音从头到尾没提，是凭"听起来像学生该有的能力"硬编的干扰项，没有原文支撑。 
 C) 原词陷阱 academic networking 把录音里多次出现的 academic（学业的）这个原词抓来拼了个新词，但录音讲的是 academic stress/success，从没说测"学业人脉"，是借原词 academic 制造的假象。  借用原文：academic stress management programs 

 D) 未提及 leadership capacities（领导力）录音里完全没出现，是又一个"听上去像能力词"的硬凑干扰，无原文依据。
questions.spoken_text: What did the new study measure in the participants?

questions.prompt: What does Patricia Pendry think traditional stress management programs may do?
options: Rid students of their anxiety.
Add to some students' stress.
Contribute little to typical students' success.
Help students with mental issues pull through.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does Patricia Pendry think traditional stress management programs may do? 

 【翻译】 Patricia Pendry认为传统压力管理项目可能会做什么? 
 A)  消除学生的焦虑。 
 B)  增加一些学生的压力。 
 C)  对普通学生的成功贡献甚微。 
 D)  帮助有心理问题的学生渡过难关。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） Add to some students' stress. 
 【定位】 P3 But they're less helpful for struggling students. Pendry believes those students may experience the programs as another lecture and feel even more stressed. 
 但对学习困难的学生而言，这些项目帮助不大。Pendry 认为这些学生可能会把这些项目当成又一堂讲座，从而感到压力更大。 

 【信号】 转折 But 后才是真实态度 。But they're less helpful for struggling students 里的 But 是关键信号——前半句先肯定"传统项目对普通学生有帮助"，But 一转才说出 Pendry 真正的判断：对困难学生反而"更有压力"。态度题的答案几乎都在转折后。 

 【替换】 feel even more stressed ↔ Add to some students' stress 感受描述→施动概括 
 for struggling students ↔ some students 下位→上位概括 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项里的 anxiety 盗用了录音 manage stress or anxiety 的原词，且 Rid\.\.\.of（彻底消除）把"帮助管理焦虑"夸大成"消除焦虑"，原文从没说传统项目能"根除"焦虑，程度被拔高了。  借用原文：manage stress or anxiety 

 C) 与原文相反 录音明说传统项目 help typical students succeed——对普通学生是有帮助的；选项却说"对普通学生的成功几乎没贡献"，把"有帮助"反成了"没帮助"，正话反说，且对象（typical students）正是录音说有用的那群人。  借用原文：these workshops help typical students succeed 

 D) 与原文相反 录音说传统项目对"有困难的学生" less helpful for struggling students——是帮不上忙；选项却说能"帮有心理问题的学生渡过难关"，把"帮不上"说成"帮得上"，方向反了，对象也被偷换成"有心理问题的学生"。  借用原文：But they're less helpful for struggling students
questions.spoken_text: What does Patricia Pendry think traditional stress management programs may do?

questions.prompt: What do entrepreneurs have to do when taking risks according to the passage?
options: Work hard and plan carefully.
Attempt to succeed at any cost.
Aim high and expect great results.
Remain optimistic even in difficulty.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do entrepreneurs have to do when taking risks according to the passage? 

 【翻译】 根据文章，企业家在承担风险时必须做什么？ 
 A)  努力工作并仔细计划。 
 B)  不惜任何代价争取成功。 
 C)  目标远大并期待卓越成果。 
 D)  即使在困难中也保持乐观。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Work hard and plan carefully. 
 【定位】 P1 On the contrary, taking risks in entrepreneurship involves careful planning and hard work. 
 恰恰相反，创业中的冒险需要的是周密的规划和辛勤的努力。 

 【信号】 转折 On the contrary 后是真意 。录音先说冒险“不是盲目去做、坐等大成果”，紧接着用 On the contrary 转折，转折之后那句 involves careful planning and hard work 才是正面答案；听到 On the contrary 就该锁定后半句。 

 【替换】 careful planning and hard work ↔ Work hard and plan carefully 名词短语换成动词短语 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 Aim high and expect great results 几乎照搬了录音被否定那半句的 expecting great results，但录音是说“冒险”不等于“盲目坐等大成果”，这是被批评的做法，不是创业者“该做”的；听到 expect great results 就选，正好踩进陷阱。  借用原文：expecting great results 

 B) 未提及 Attempt to succeed at any cost“不惜一切代价求成功”，录音通篇没说要“不计代价”，反而强调冒险要靠规划和努力、还提醒“并非所有风险都是好风险”，这种太满的说法是命题人添加的。 
 D) 答非所问 Remain optimistic even in difficulty 式的“乐观”确实在录音里出现过，an optimistic risk-taker 也提到 optimistic，adapting in difficult times 也讲困境中应变，但那是讲“失败时的心态”，不是回答“冒险时必须做什么”这道题，把别处的内容搬来作答即错位。  借用原文：an optimistic risk-taker
questions.spoken_text: What do entrepreneurs have to do when taking risks according to the passage?

questions.prompt: What does the passage say is key to business growth?
options: Regarding failure as something inevitable.
Trying out innovative marketing strategies.
Venturing into sectors never explored before.
Being willing to experiment with novel ideas.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say is key to business growth? 

 【翻译】 文章认为什么是业务增长的关键？ 
 A)  将失败视为不可避免的事情。 
 B)  尝试创新的营销策略。 
 C)  冒险进入从未探索过的领域。 
 D)  愿意尝试新颖的想法。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Being willing to experiment with novel ideas. 
 【定位】 P2 The willingness to experiment with new ideas is key to business growth. 
 愿意去尝试新点子，是企业成长的关键。 

 【信号】 原文 key 与题干同词对应 。录音 is key to business growth 和题干 key to business growth 用词几乎一模一样，这句话主语 The willingness to experiment with new ideas 就是答案；标志词 key 一响，定位即成。 

 【替换】 The willingness to experiment with new ideas ↔ Being willing to experiment with novel ideas 近义改写 new=novel 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 Trying out innovative marketing strategies 听起来很像“创新”，录音确有“new ideas”的意思，但根本没提“marketing strategies（营销策略）”；它用“创新”诱你，却塞了原文没有的“营销”。 
 C) 过度推断 Venturing into sectors never explored before“进入从未有人涉足的领域”比录音的“尝试新点子”程度重得多，录音只说 experiment with new ideas，并没说要闯入“全新行业”，这是把原意拔高了。  借用原文：experiment with new ideas 

 A) 原词陷阱 Regarding failure as something inevitable 里 failure 是录音高频词，look at failure as an opportunity to learn 也讲了对失败的看法，但录音说的是“把失败当学习机会”，不是“把失败当不可避免”，更不是回答“增长关键”；它用熟悉的 failure 制造错觉。  借用原文：look at failure as an opportunity to learn
questions.spoken_text: What does the passage say is key to business growth?

questions.prompt: What are we advised to do when we fail?
options: Expect future success so as to move forward.
Learn from our failure and forge ahead.
Distinguish between good and bad risks.
Examine our strategies and find out weaknesses.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are we advised to do when we fail? 

 【翻译】 当我们失败时，建议我们做什么？ 
 A)  期待未来成功以便继续前进。 
 B)  从失败中学习并勇往直前。 
 C)  区分好的风险和坏的风险。 
 D)  检查我们的策略并找出弱点。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Learn from our failure and forge ahead. 
 【定位】 P2 But just remember that not all risks are good ones, and when you fail, learn from it and move forward. 
 但要记住，并非所有风险都是好风险；当你失败时，要从中吸取教训，然后继续前进。 

 【信号】 条件句 when you fail 直接应题 。题干问 when we fail，录音正好有 when you fail, learn from it and move forward 这句条件句，措辞与题干对应；听到 when you fail 后面紧跟的 learn from it and move forward 就是答案。 

 【替换】 learn from it and move forward ↔ Learn from our failure and forge ahead 代词还原＋近义短语 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Expect future success so as to move forward 借用了录音的 move forward，但把前提偷换成“指望未来成功”——录音让你“前进”的前提是“从失败中学”，不是“指望成功”；听到 move forward 就选，正中陷阱。  借用原文：move forward 

 C) 答非所问 Distinguish between good and bad risks 用了录音 not all risks are good ones 的意思，录音确实提醒“并非所有风险都好”，但那是另一层提醒，不是“失败时”被建议做的事，答非所问。  借用原文：not all risks are good ones 

 D) 未提及 Examine our strategies and find out weaknesses“检查策略、找出弱点”录音没有对应说法，录音只讲“失败教你如何战略性思考”think and plan strategically，并没有让你去“查弱点”，是凭 strategically 一词联想出来的。  借用原文：think and plan strategically
questions.spoken_text: What are we advised to do when we fail?

questions.prompt: What does it mean to risk-taking businesses when most people tend to avoid risk?
options: Fresher offers.
Safer operation.
More challenges.
Less competition.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does it mean to risk-taking businesses when most people tend to avoid risk? 

 【翻译】 当大多数人倾向于规避风险时，对承担风险的企业意味着什么？ 
 A)  更新鲜的机会。 
 B)  更安全的运营。 
 C)  更多挑战。 
 D)  更少竞争。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Less competition. 
 【定位】 P3 Simply put, when most individuals stay away from risk, it means less competition for risk-takers. 
 简单地说，当大多数人远离风险时，对冒险者而言就意味着更少的竞争。 

 【信号】 Simply put 总结句给结论 。录音用 Simply put（简而言之）领出一句总结，it means less competition for risk-takers 直接给出结论，与题干“what does it mean”正好对接；听到 Simply put 这类收束词就知道结论要来了。 

 【替换】 less competition for risk-takers ↔ Less competition 几乎原词截取 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Fresher offers 借了录音 fresh offers 这个原词，但那句讲的是冒险者“用新点子、新供给、大胆发明在立标准”，是描述冒险者的做法，不是回答“别人避险意味着什么”，张冠李戴。  借用原文：fresh offers 

 C) 与原文相反 More challenges“更多挑战”与录音结论方向相反：录音说别人避险对冒险者是“更少竞争”这种好事，而 challenge 是偏负面的负担，录音的 adapting in difficult times 谈的是冒险者善应变，并没说“更多挑战”。  借用原文：adapting in difficult times 

 B) 未提及 Safer operation 像是从录音 stay safe 联想来的，但 as long as you want to stay safe 是说“你若一味求稳就永远不会知道结果”，是对“守成者”的提醒，并不是说冒险企业能“更安全地运营”，原文没有这层意思。  借用原文：stay safe
questions.spoken_text: What does it mean to risk taking businesses when most people tend to avoid risk?
